This page corresponds to O*NET 31-1132.00 Orderlies; the core is assisting patients in hospitals, per the care team's instructions, to transfer from bed to wheelchair, stretcher, or examination table and transporting them to operating rooms, imaging rooms, and other locations; they may also restock supplies, clean, or move equipment.

paragraphs: Core process: Confirm the patient, destination, and transport requirements; check mobility, fall risk, line and tube, and isolation requirements; check the safety status of wheelchairs, stretchers, and brakes; transfer patients safely according to training and staffing requirements.
Mostly works between hospital wards, operating rooms, and imaging departments, requiring considerable walking, lifting, and close patient contact, and may work shifts.
Common tools and systems: wheelchairs, stretchers, mobile beds, transfer assist devices, personal protective equipment, and patient transport records.

Compared with adjacent roles, this occupation centers on hospital patient transfer and in-hospital transport, equipment and environment cleaning, and supply support, and may also assist with daily activities depending on the division of duties; it does not independently diagnose, administer medication, or develop care plans, and psychiatric aides belong to another U.S. occupational classification.
Qualified delivery must demonstrate: identity and destination verification, pre-transport risk confirmation, equipment safety checks, arrival handover, and anomaly records.

Nursing assistants mainly perform daily living assistance and basic care; this occupation focuses more on patient transfer and in-hospital transport, does not independently diagnose, administer medication, or develop care plans; psychiatric aides belong to another U.S. occupational classification.
Psychiatric aides focus on assisting the life and activities of mental health patients, with different occupational tasks and training.
Home health aides lean toward in-home personal care; look at the final output rather than similar titles.
Difference between nursing assistants and this occupation: orderlies focus more on in-hospital transfer and transport.
Choosing nursing assistant work suits those who prefer continuous bedside care.
Explorer
Use fictional samples to learn about receiving instructions.
Incumbent
Check identity and destination verification, pre-transport risk confirmation, equipment safety checks, arrival handover, and anomaly records, and observe authorization.
Crew lead
Check whether tool records match on-site identity, equipment, and transport handover; patient movement must be trained and authorized, and clinical anomalies go to the care team.
Career changer
Moving to nursing or emergency care requires separate education and licensure training; in-hospital transport experience does not automatically grant clinical judgment or operating authority.

values: O01 paper transport sheet identifies T1 / birth code D1 and destination imaging room; fictional wristband T1/D2. Rule: the two identifiers and the destination must agree; verify only the records, list the hold and rescue questions, and do not guess or change the birth code.

O02 the two identifiers and destination agree; the equipment record shows a brake fault, the recipient field is blank, and the appointment time has arrived. Rule: a fault or missing recipient that is unresolved cannot be marked transportable; list the transfer questions, and do not repair the equipment or move the patient yourself.

O01 the second identifier conflicts, so keep both original values and hand them to authorized care staff to verify identity and destination; for O02 register the fault and the missing recipient separately, ask authorized personnel to handle the equipment and confirm receipt, and do not release based on the appointment. Both cases remain unresolved, which is not a judgment that the patient is clinically stable.
Submit O01/O02 two lines: the two identifiers, destination, equipment status, recipient, conflicts and missing items, and hold and transfer questions.
O01 records D1/D2 are not guessed; O02 keeps the fault and the blank field, and it is not marked transportable until simulated authorization feedback arrives; no real patient is recorded.
Also submit an anomaly transfer form and a simulated handover draft, listing the original values, pending questions, proposed responsible person, and simulated review feedback.
Corrections must keep the original records and basis; paper verification must not be treated as certification in safe lifting, line and tube handling, or clinical training.

career_risk_cards.heading: Main risks for hospital orderlies (patient transport)

risks.mitigation: Use safe transfer procedures and request assistance.
risks.scenario: Wheels are not locked or patient ability is not assessed before transfer.
risks.title: Fall injury

risks.affected_roles: Hospital orderly (patient transport) positions that carry out line and tube dislodgement related tasks and record handover
risks.consequence: May interrupt treatment or cause patient harm.
risks.mitigation: Verify lines and tubes before transport and follow clinical staff guidance.
risks.scenario: Infusion or oxygen lines are ignored during transfer.
risks.title: Line and tube dislodgement

risks.affected_roles: Hospital orderly (patient transport) positions that carry out identity error related tasks and record handover
risks.consequence: May send the patient to the wrong examination or treatment location.
risks.mitigation: Verify dual identifiers and hand over.
risks.scenario: Wristband and destination are not verified.
risks.title: Identity error

risks.affected_roles: Hospital orderly (patient transport) positions that carry out infection transmission related tasks and record handover
risks.consequence: May increase infection exposure for patients and staff.
risks.scenario: Isolation measures or equipment cleaning are inadequate.
risks.title: Infection transmission

risks.affected_roles: Hospital orderly (patient transport) positions that carry out occupational injury related tasks and record handover
risks.consequence: May cause musculoskeletal injuries such as lower back injuries in lifting personnel.
risks.mitigation: Use assist devices and seek help from multiple people.
risks.scenario: A single person lifts beyond safe capacity.
risks.title: Occupational injury

risks.affected_roles: Hospital orderly (patient transport) positions that carry out condition deterioration related tasks and record handover
risks.consequence: May delay clinical assessment and emergency handling.
risks.mitigation: Stop transport immediately and notify the care team.
risks.scenario: An anomaly during transport is not escalated.
risks.title: Condition deterioration

subject.name: Hospital orderly (patient transport)
subject.summary: Assist patients in hospitals, per the care team's instructions, to transfer from bed to wheelchair, stretcher, or examination table and transport them to operating rooms, imaging rooms, and other locations; may also restock supplies, clean, or move equipment.
